title: Day 7 — CSV Tokenizer Edge Cases
prompt: We ingest user-uploaded CSVs. Right now we just split each line on commas and it breaks on real spreadsheets. Parse a single CSV record into fields correctly. How do you approach it?

clarifications.answer: Yes — a field can be wrapped in double quotes, and inside quotes a comma is literal text, not a separator. Strip the wrapping quotes from the result.
Inside a quoted field, two double-quotes "" mean one literal double-quote character.
Whitespace is significant — do not trim. ' b ' stays ' b '.
Empty fields are allowed. A trailing comma produces a trailing empty field, and an empty line is a single empty field.
Just one record (one line) per call for this exercise — no embedded newlines to worry about.
You can try, but think about the escaped-quote case before you commit to a regex.

hints: Think of it as a state machine with two states: inside-quotes and outside-quotes.
Scan character by character. Outside quotes: a comma ends the field, a quote enters quoted mode. Inside quotes: a quote might close the field OR be the first of an escaped pair.
When inside quotes and you see a quote, peek at the next char: if it's also a quote, emit one quote and skip both; otherwise close the quoted section.
